subject: general
question: Which of the following was a major criticism of the Green Revolution in India?

options.text: It led to regional and crop imbalances.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It led to regional and crop imbalances.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Green Revolution** in India, initiated in the 1960s, focused on increasing agricultural production through the use of **high-yield variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation technologies**.
 
• While it significantly increased food grain production, it led to **regional imbalances**. The benefits were concentrated in regions like **Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh**, while other regions like Eastern and Southern India were relatively neglected.
 
• It also caused **crop imbalances** by emphasizing the production of certain crops, primarily **wheat and rice**. This sidelined other crops, including pulses and coarse grains, which are essential for nutritional security and crop diversity.
